hints: The bisector has gradient $-3$, so the line $AB$ has gradient $m_{AB} = \dfrac{1}{3}$.
Write the line $AB$ through $A(7, 2)$ as $y - 2 = \dfrac{1}{3}(x - 7) \implies x - 3y = 1$.
The midpoint $M$ is the intersection of line $AB$ and the perpendicular bisector $y = -3x + 8$.
walkthrough:
The bisector crosses the segment exactly at its midpoint.
Find the gradient of line $AB$ from the bisector gradient $m_{\text{perp}} = -3$:
$$m_{AB} = -\dfrac{1}{-3} = \dfrac{1}{3}$$

Write the equation of line $AB$ passing through $A(7, 2)$:
$$y - 2 = \dfrac{1}{3}(x - 7) \implies 3y - 6 = x - 7 \implies x - 3y = 1$$
$$y = \dfrac{1}{3}x - \dfrac{1}{3}$$

Find the intersection point $M$ of line $AB$ with the perpendicular bisector $y = -3x + 8$:
$$\dfrac{1}{3}x - \dfrac{1}{3} = -3x + 8$$
$$\dfrac{10}{3}x = \dfrac{25}{3} \implies 10x = 25 \implies x = \dfrac{5}{2}$$
$$y = -3\left(\dfrac{5}{2}\right) + 8 = -\dfrac{15}{2} + \dfrac{16}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
$$M\left(\dfrac{5}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$$

hints: Use midpoint equations: $\dfrac{7 + x_B}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2} \implies x_B = -2$ and $\dfrac{2 + y_B}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies y_B = -1$.
walkthrough:
The bisector crosses the segment exactly at its midpoint.
Apply the midpoint coordinate formula with $A(7, 2)$ and $M\left(\dfrac{5}{2}, \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$:
$$\dfrac{7 + x_B}{2} = \dfrac{5}{2} \implies 7 + x_B = 5 \implies x_B = -2$$
$$\dfrac{2 + y_B}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies 2 + y_B = 1 \implies y_B = -1$$
$$B(-2, -1)$$
